title: Publish from Revit (beta) | Verse Engine by Ctruh
description: Publish a scene from Revit to a shareable link with Verse Engine by Ctruh. Step-by-step guide to install, publish and share.

docs.article:
Publish from Revit#

**Status: 4.0.0-beta.1 — builds against the Revit 2024 and 2025 API, needs a real Revit install.** The add-in compiles for .NET Framework 4.8 (Revit 2021–2024, against the 2024 API) and .NET 8 (Revit 2025+, against the 2025 API) with 0 errors. Its glTF writer's textured test cube passes the Khronos glTF-Validator with 0 errors and 0 warnings and builds on a real Verse server; the shared C# upload helper published GLB, OBJ (with units) and IFC, one-shot and resumable, and handled a dead server and a cancel (web/test/fix-verify-aec.mjs). The export of a real Revit model — tessellation, materials, links, the ribbon — has **not been run inside Revit** yet.

A Verse ribbon tab with Publish to Verse: the active 3D view is walked by Revit's own tessellator and written as a binary glTF — one node per element, so a click in the Verse link names the wall, door or family and its level — with PBR materials from the render appearance. It uploads with progress and gives you a streaming share link, copied and opened.

You need: Windows with Revit 2021–2024 (use build/net48) or 2025+ (use build/net8.0-windows).

1. Install#

Download VersePublish-Revit-4.0.0-beta.1.zip from the downloads page once the packages are published, or build it (any OS with the .NET 8 SDK):

Code
sh integrations/aec/revit/make_package.sh   # -> integrations/aec/revit/dist/VersePublish-Revit-4.0.0-beta.1.zip

From the zip, copy VersePublishRevit.dll and VersePublish.addin from the folder matching your Revit (build/net48/ or build/net8.0-windows/) into %APPDATA%\Autodesk\Revit\Addins\<year>\. Start Revit and accept the "load add-in" prompt once.

2. Server and key#

Verse ▸ Settings: server URL (default https://verse.ctruh.com), API key, account token (from Studio), bake lighting on the server (no / preview / final), tessellation detail 0–15, embed textures, open the link when done, and Use this server and key for every Verse plug-in.

Nothing is compiled in. Settings live in the per-user file every Verse plug-in shares, %APPDATA%\Ctruh\VersePublish\settings.json, in its revit section (or shared when you tick "every plug-in"). A 4.0.0-beta.1 Revit settings file at that path is read as-is. VERSE_SERVER, VERSE_API_KEY and VERSE_TOKEN in the environment override the file — handy on a render farm.

3. Publish#

  1. Open a 3D view (the {3D} view is fine).
  2. Verse ▸ Publish to Verse. A window shows Exporting… N elements, then the upload %, then the server's build stages. Cancel works in every phase and tells you whether anything was published.
  3. The Published dialog shows the link; it is on the clipboard and opens in the browser.

Success looks like: the Published dialog shows the link (also on the clipboard, and opened in the browser); the model opens upright, in metres, and clicking a wall names it.

Files over 100 MB use the resumable upload: a dropped connection continues where the server got to.

What gets exported#

  • Geometry: every visible element in the view, through Revit's CustomExporter / IExportContext; family instances and Revit links keep their transforms. Feet → metres; Z-up → glTF Y-up.
  • Materials: render-appearance colour, transparency, metal flag, glossiness → roughness; for Generic appearances, the base-colour bitmap at its real-world scale. If texture files are not found, the summary says so — set VERSE_REVIT_TEXTURE_PATHS (semicolon-separated) to your Additional render appearance paths.
  • Element data: each node carries the Revit element id and category, so the link can name what was clicked.
  • Not exported: RPC content (trees, people), lights — set Bake to let the server light the scene.

Troubleshooting#

Every problem ends in one sentence; the first words tell you which row applies.

You seeWhat it meansDo this
"Could not reach the Verse server at …"Wrong server URL, no internet, or a firewall / proxy blocking the plug-in.Check Server URL in Verse ▸ Settings (default https://verse.ctruh.com) and open it in a browser.
"The Verse server at … did not recognise the account token …"The token is mistyped, was revoked, or belongs to another server. Nothing was uploaded.Copy the token again from Studio, or clear it to publish without an account.
"The server did not accept your API key or account token …"This server only takes uploads with an API key; the sentence ends with its reason.Enter the key from the server's operator in Verse ▸ Settings.
"Upload limit reached: …"The hourly upload limit, or the API key's daily quota.Wait as the sentence says, or add an account token from Studio (a higher limit).
"The server is busy right now. …" / "The server is out of storage. …"The server's build queue or disk is full. Your file is fine.Publish again in a few minutes.
"The upload kept failing …"The connection dropped again and again.Publish again when the connection is steady; a large upload continues where it stopped.
"Verse cannot build … files yet. Export the model as GLB (or FBX / OBJ) and publish that file instead."STEP / IGES / native CAD files are not built by the server yet.Export GLB (or FBX / OBJ) and publish that.
"Stopped waiting for the server. The scene is still being built …"You cancelled after the upload; the server keeps building.The scene appears in your Verse dashboard (with an account token) when it is ready.
"This project has no 3D view to export. Open or create a 3D view and publish again."Publishing exports a 3D view.Open {3D} (or any 3D view) first.
"The 3D view has no visible geometry to publish. …"Everything in the view is hidden or cut away.Check the view's visibility settings and section box.
No Verse tab after starting RevitRevit did not load the add-in (wrong folder or the wrong build for your Revit year).VersePublishRevit.dll + VersePublish.addin from build/net48 (2021–2024) or build/net8.0-windows (2025+) in %APPDATA%\Autodesk\Revit\Addins\<year>\; answer Always Load.

Anything else: send the whole sentence (and, for a build error, the scene name) to hello@ctruh.com.

What has been tested#

dotnet build: net48 against the Revit 2024 API, net8.0-windows against the 2025 APItested
GLB writer: textured cube → Khronos glTF-Validator 0 errors / 0 warnings; the server builds ittested
Shared C# helper → real server (GLB / OBJ+units / IFC, one-shot + resumable, scene done and opening, dead server, cancel)tested
Settings file shared with the Python and Ruby plug-instested
Export of a real model, ribbon, dialogs inside Revitneeds a real install
